en: Points of Controversy The Great Fifty The Sixteenth Chapter
The Discussion on Form Belonging to the Fine-Material and Immaterial Spheres:
Is there form that belongs to the fine-material sphere? Yes.

Is it associated with the attainment-aimed-at, the rebirth-aimed-at, and the pleasant dwelling in this very life; and is it accompanied by, co-arisen with, conjoined with, and associated with the mind aimed at attainment, the mind aimed at rebirth, and the mind of pleasant dwelling in this very life—
arising together, ceasing together, having the same basis, and having the same object?

It should not be stated thus … [as before] … Is it not the case that [this state] is not to be attained through meditative absorption, not to be attained through rebirth, and not a pleasant dwelling in this very life;
and that it is not accompanied by a mind to be attained through meditative absorption, nor by a mind to be attained through rebirth, nor by a mind for a pleasant dwelling in this very life?
Is it co-nascent, conjoined, associated, of one arising, one cessation, one basis, and one object?
Yes.

If it is not to be attained through meditative absorption, not to be attained at rebirth, and not a pleasant abiding in this very life, then [it is] not by means of a mind that is to be attained through meditative absorption... [and so on].
It has a single object; yet, indeed, it should not be said that "there is form belonging to the fine-material sphere.
Is there form belonging to the immaterial sphere?
Yes. [It is] that which pertains to attainment, that which pertains to rebirth, and the pleasant dwelling in this very life;
it is accompanied by, co-arisen with, conjoined with, and associated with the mind pertaining to attainment, the mind pertaining to rebirth, and the mind of the pleasant dwelling in this very life.
[Are they] of one arising, one cessation, one basis, and one object?
One should not say so... [etc.

...Is it not the case that this is neither to be attained through meditative absorption, nor to be attained upon rebirth, nor a pleasant dwelling in this very life; and that it is not by means of a mind to be attained through meditative absorption... [etc.]?
Is it a single object? Yes.
If so, then it is not something to be attained through meditative absorption, nor is it something to be attained through rebirth... [and so forth].
It has a single basis and a single object; indeed, it should not be said that "there is form belonging to the formless realm.
It should not be so stated.
“Is there matter belonging to the fine-material sphere, and is there matter belonging to the immaterial sphere?”—
“Yes.”—
“But is not matter belonging to the sense-sphere because it has been produced by karma belonging to the sense-sphere?”
“Yes. “If, by the performance of sense-sphere karma, matter is of the sense sphere, then indeed, sir,
you must admit that by the performance of fine-material-sphere karma, matter is of the fine-material sphere, and by the performance of immaterial-sphere karma, matter is of the immaterial sphere.”
The discussion concerning the limits of the fine-material and immaterial spheres regarding form is finished.
